test.name: Suggests a missing_parents hole from a surveyed tree
test.description: tree_gaps returns exactly one hole, of type missing_parents. The agent should check what FamilySearch has for it and suggest that one person with a single-fact research question.

input.delegation:
What should I research in my tree?

personId: TGAP-ROT

judge_context: This is the direct-agent arm: no routing skill is staged, and the delegation is relayed verbatim. No project exists in this test, so the agent must not look for research.json, create a project, or call any writer tool (it holds none).

tree_gaps returns ONE hole: Hannah Pruitt (TGAP-GM2): both parents missing; a birth/baptism around 1860-1864 in Lancaster, Pennsylvania. The agent should call tree_gaps with personId TGAP-ROT and defaults, then check what FamilySearch has (person_record_matches, person_quality, record_search, collections_search) for that hole. The catch-all fixtures return empty results; an empty check is a result, not a fault, and the agent should still suggest the hole, saying plainly that nothing further was found.

The suggestion must name Hannah Pruitt / TGAP-GM2 and carry ONE research question that is a single fact, names the person, and scopes place and years, e.g. 'Who were the parents of Hannah Pruitt, born about 1862 in Lancaster, Pennsylvania?'. A question that spans several facts or the whole family is a fail.
The agent's return should end with the summary_for_user block: a `---` line followed by plain prose with no label, and no identifiers, file names, tool names or field names in it.
